prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1145; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The vehicle presents front-end damage consistent with a low-speed head-on impact, including a cracked bumper cover, a bent radiator support, and a damaged hood latch area. The pattern of crush and the location of the contact points line up with the account given for how the collision occurred. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior records or inspection. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover, hood, and radiator support, followed by refinishing and a standard alignment check. The labor hours submitted fit the scope of this work. The invoices reviewed show no repeated charges for the same operation.
